Hi Jamie — thanks for the note and attachments. Short answer: generally yes, we accept vendor redacted summaries for SIG/CAIQ as long as they include a clear scope statement and vendor attestation, and the vendor credentials show a recent engagement date and relevant cloud/SaaS experience.

A few specifics our security team usually requires to satisfy customers and auditors:
- Engagement firm name and point of contact (we'll want to validate via email)
- Engagement completion date (month/year)
- Scope statement listing systems/environments tested (redactions are fine if they indicate "production/internal infra" vs "test environment")
- High-level categories of findings (e.g., "auth bypass, XSS, privilege escalation") — exploit PoCs can be redacted
- Current remediation status (fixed / mitigated / accepted) and a date for fixes where available

If the summary includes those items and the vendor provides a one-page attestation (signed) plus a firm CV, our SOC/assurance reviewers typically mark it acceptable for SIG evidence. For procurement exceptions we sometimes need the unredacted workpapers under an NDA to validate critical/high severity fix claims; that happens about 10% of the time for large enterprise deals.

I'm looping in Marissa and Karthik to confirm we don't need additional artifacts for Acme's specific SIG requirements.

— Sofia
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sofia / Karthik — quick internal notes:
- Vendor credibility: BlackBox Security appears on our approved vendor list; they completed a SOC 2-aligned pen test for another customer in 2026 Q2. I'll attach their vendor creds to the shared drive link (summary only).
- Report age: we require tests within 12 months for SIG/CAIQ evidence. If the engagement date is older than that, we ask for either a re-test or a documented reason (e.g., minimal change window + additional compensating controls).
- Retest policy: for critical findings that were patched less than 30 days prior to the audit, we usually require remediation verification (either re-test or mitigation evidence). For high/medium findings we accept vendor attestations with remediation timelines up to 90 days, but prefer a follow-up verification within 6 months for enterprise customers.

For Acme specifically (they're asking for redacted only): ask BlackBox to include engagement date and a line-item remediation status tied to each high/critical finding. If they can't provide PoCs, have them include the root cause classification + fix date. If they sign an NDA we can request limited unredacted workpapers for our assurance review.

Mina — any objections to offering Acme the redacted-summary + attestation route with a note that we may request workpapers under NDA if needed?

-Marissa
Senior Security Engineer
